doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: Club date union scale pay
summary: After five years in DC he returned to New York in 1980; Local 802 scale for a four-hour Saturday club date rose from $96 to about $200.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Can I ask you one thing about that? Do you recall the pay scale for those, are you talking about maybe in the 80s?

Yeah. When I came back, after I went to college I went to DC for five years and was there for five years and then I came back to New York in 1980 and I started just, because it was work I made some phone calls and I started doing these club dates in addition to

whatever jazz playing I was doing, rehearsing with bands or playing little jazz gigs, or I started putting together my own nonet. But I remember in 1980 for a four hour Saturday night club date the scale was 96 dollars. By the time I quit doing those gigs, about in the early 90s the scale was up to about 200 dollars for a Saturday night.
Yeah. That’s a Local 802 club date scale for a four hour Saturday night. Four hour continuous as they say.

Now if a person, if a young woman calls you and says, “I’m getting married, I got your name, can you play” — and all the details. Is this something that you were required to go through the union to do?
